ai.title: Disable Helicone rate limit policy in backend API clients
ai.summary: Helicone rate limit policy disabled in Claude and OpenAI API clients by commenting out the `Helicone-RateLimit-Policy` header. This change affects `backend/src/claude.ts` and `backend/src/openai-api.ts`. The `RATE_LIMIT_POLICY` constant remains defined but is no longer sent in request headers.

eli5.text: The software stopped asking its helper service to limit how fast requests get sent. You wouldn't notice anything different while using the assistant; behind the scenes, the rate-limit instruction is now turned off for both the Claude and OpenAI connections.

ai.title: Add error handling to knowledge file generation
ai.summary: Added `.catch()` blocks to `generateKnowledgeFiles` in `backend/src/generate-knowledge-files.ts` and `mainPrompt` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This prevents unhandled promise rejections during file processing and knowledge generation, logging errors via `logger.error` and returning null or empty arrays respectively. Scope limited to backend logic. Internal stability improvement.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to turn your files into its knowledge base, it now catches and quietly logs errors instead of crashing the whole process. This only affects the backend system that handles knowledge file generation, so you won't see any difference in features or performance. It's a behind-the-scenes stability improvement that prevents unhandled errors from interrupting internal file processing.

ai.title: npm update script now detects nvm installs
ai.summary: The `detectInstaller` function in `npm-app/src/update-manicode.ts` now recognizes paths containing `.nvm` as global npm installations. This fixes an issue where Freebuff installed via nvm was misidentified, preventing the update script from running correctly. The change is internal to the CLI update mechanism.

eli5.text: The program that keeps your command-line tools up to date had a blind spot: it didn't recognize when software was installed through a popular tool called nvm, which many developers use to manage different versions of Node.js. This meant the updater would sometimes fail to detect what you had installed, leading to incorrect behavior when trying to update. The detection logic has been fixed so it now correctly identifies nvm-installed software as a global installation, allowing the update process to work as expected. This fix takes effect immediately as part of the regular update that gets installed automatically.

ai.title: Lower CLI large-file change threshold to 8000
ai.summary: The CLI in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` now uses `8_000` instead of `4 * 10_000` as the length threshold for including file change patches. This reduces the maximum size of user edits included in messages, replacing longer patches with `[LARGE_FILE_CHANGE_TOO_LONG_TO_REPRODUCE]`. The change affects the CLI's file change processing logic.

eli5.text: When you make a very large edit to a file, the assistant now receives a shorter placeholder message instead of the full details of your change. This affects edits that exceed the new size limit, which was lowered to reduce how much data gets sent in a single message. If you were to look, you would notice a cap on the size of file changes that appear in full, with anything bigger replaced by a notice that the change was too long to reproduce. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to keep message sizes manageable, and it is live today.

ai.title: Fix editfile closing tag typo in createFileBlock
ai.summary: Corrected a malformed closing tag in `createFileBlock` and `createFileBlockWithoutPath`. The output now emits `</edit_file>` instead of `</edit_file>`. This ensures the agent parser correctly identifies file edit boundaries. Scope limited to `common/src/util/file.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a file, it sends a special tagged message to mark where the file content starts and ends. One of those end tags had a typo that made the assistant unable to recognize where the edit stopped, so edits could get cut off or run together. That typo is now fixed, so the assistant can correctly read and apply file edits as intended.

ai.title: Add file access validation in project files
ai.summary: getFiles in npm-app/src/project-files.ts now validates paths against projectRoot and .gitignore rules. Returns [FILE_OUTSIDE_PROJECT] or [FILE_IGNORED] markers instead of file content. parseGitignore exported from common/src/project-file-tree.ts to support shared logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to read files in your project, it now checks whether each file actually lives inside your project folder and respects your ignore rules (like the contents of your.gitignore file). Files that are outside the project boundary return a marker saying so instead of their contents, and files that match an ignore rule return a different marker. This means the assistant will no longer silently read files you've told it to ignore, so you can keep private or generated files out of its view.

ai.title: Bump manicode version to 1.0.97
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.97 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release increment. No functional changes.

eli5.text: If you reinstalled the assistant today, you'd get a fresh copy stamped 1.0.97 that now shows a credit usage range on the pricing page (an intense one-hour session uses 500-1000 credits), routes API requests without the old rate-limit header, validates file access before reading project files, and includes a few small fixes like better error handling when generating knowledge files. These changes are live now and apply to anyone who pulls the updated package.

ai.title: Improve cross-platform command error detection
ai.summary: Updated `handleRunTerminalCommand` in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` to detect Linux-specific 'not found' and capitalized 'Syntax error:' messages alongside existing Mac/Windows patterns. This ensures accurate error reporting across platforms.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a command in a terminal and that command fails, it now spots the specific kind of 'command not found' or 'syntax error' message that shows up on Linux systems, in addition to the ones it already recognized from macOS and Windows. This means error reports are now accurate no matter which operating system you're using. If you looked, you'd see the assistant give more precise feedback when a command fails on Linux, instead of misreading the error or flagging the wrong issue.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.98
ai.summary: Version field updated from 1.0.97 to 1.0.98 in npm-app/package.json. No functional changes or dependency updates included in this commit.

eli5.text: Updating the assistant to version 1.0.98 lets you get clearer, more helpful messages when something goes wrong while running commands, and it stops the system from occasionally slowing things down or stopping unexpectedly. The update also makes it easier for the assistant to work with files in your project, including catching issues with how files are accessed and fixing small mistakes that could break things. These improvements are live today for anyone using the assistant, with better handling of errors, smoother operation, and more reliable file management.
